data.headline: Your cassava may have bacterial blight
data.whatsHappening: Bacteria are making brown, angular spots on the leaves, and some shoots are drying from the tip.
data.whyItMatters: It spreads through cuttings, tools and rain splash. Left alone it moves across the field and cuts your harvest.
steps: Pull out plants with drying shoots and burn them away from the field.
Don’t take cuttings from this field for planting.
Clean your hoe and panga after working here.
Next season, plant clean cuttings of a resistant variety — your farmer promoter can help you find them.

evidence.lookFor: Sticky gum on stems — look for it
signs: Angular brown spots between leaf veins

sources: Rwanda Agriculture Board (RAB) crop protection guidance
